newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-SRNICEK MISTAKE HANDS METZ UEFA CUP CHANCE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SRNICEK MISTAKE HANDS METZ UEFA CUP CHANCE.

text.p: English premier league leaders Newcastle threw away what looked like a probable victory when their Czech goalkeeper Pavel Srnicek committed another in a career-long series of errors to give Metz a 1-1 draw in their UEFA Cup third round, first leg tie on Tuesday.
Leading 1-0 from a first-half Peter Beardsley penalty, Srnicek committed his mistake in the 66th minute when he raced off his line to cut out a cross from his right.
But he totally mis-judged the flight of the ball and was off-balance in mid-air and powerless to prevent Sengalese striker Amara Traore from sending his back-header looping into the net.
Newcastle took the lead in the 32nd minute when Metz goalkeeper Lionel Letizi tripped Colombian striker Faustino Asprilia allowing captain Peter Beardsley to score from the spot.
Newcastle, without their 21.0 million pounds ($35.1 million) twin strike-force of Alan Shearer and Les Ferdinand, were made to battle hard for their lead on a sodden pitch.
Metz's Brazilian striker Isaias was booked soon after the goal for punching David Batty, who left the pitch briefly with blood pouring from over his left eye to receive treatment.
Metz, who had never appeared in the third round of an European competition before, eventually equalised through Traore.
The French side kept pushing until the final whistle but Newcastle held on to a draw which leaves them with a reasonable chance of qualifying for the quarter-finals in two weeks at St James' Park.
